State Law reference— Local alcoholic beverages licenses, O.C.G.A. § 3-3-2 et seq.; local regulation of distilled spirits, O.C.G.A. § 3-3-40 et seq.; local regulation of malt beverages, O.C.G.A. § 3-5-40 et seq.; local regulation of wine O.C.G.A. § 3-6-40; public drunkenness, O.C.G.A. § 16-11-41.
125:
This chapter has been enacted in accordance with a plan designed for the purposes, among others, of promoting the health and general welfare of the community, to establish reasonable and ascertainable standards for the regulation and control of the licensing and sale of alcoholic beverages, to protect, and preserve schools and churches, to give effect to existing land use and to preserve certain residential areas, with reasonable consideration, among others, to the character of the areas and their peculiar suitability for particular uses, the congestion in the roads and streets, and with a general view of promoting desirable living conditions and sustaining stability of neighborhood and property values, and to protect against the evils of concentration of the retail outlets for distilled spirits in one family or to prevent undesirable persons from engaging in or having any interest in alcoholic beverages.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
126:
Alcohol means ethyl alcohol, hydrated oxide of ethyl or spirits of wine, from whatever source or by whatever process produced.
Alcoholic beverage means and includes all alcohol, distilled spirits, beer, malt beverage, wine, or fortified wine.
Beer or malt beverage means any alcoholic beverage obtained by any fermentation of any infusion or decoction of barley, malt, hops, or any other similar product, or any combination of such products in water containing not more than 14 percent alcohol by volume, including ale, porter, brown, stout, lager beer, small beer, and strong beer. The term "malt beverage" does not include sake, known as Japanese rice wine.
Board of commissioners means the Board of Commissioners of Lincoln County, Georgia.
Brewer means a manufacturer, maker, producer, or bottler of malt beverages according to the definition provided in O.C.G.A. § 3-1-2, as may be amended from time to time.
Brewpub means any eating establishment in which beer or malt beverages are manufactured or brewed, subject to the barrel production limitation prescribed in O.C.G.A. § 3-5-36, as may be amended from time to time, for retail consumption on premises and solely in draft form.
Church building means the main structure used by any religious organization for purposes of worship and the surrounding property or campus directly incorporated into such use in compliance with the zoning ordinances of the county.
Community development means the Community Development Division of the Public Works Department of Lincoln County.
County shall mean the unincorporated areas of Lincoln County, Georgia.
Distilled spirits means any alcoholic beverage obtained by distillation or containing more than 21 percent alcohol by volume, including, but not limited to, all fortified wines.
Eating establishment or restaurant means a business establishment which sells prepared food for consumption on the premises, with a full service kitchen offering food service every hour such establishment is open and deriving at least 50 percent of its total annual gross sales from the sale of prepared food items which shall not include the sale of any alcoholic beverages. Any other eating establishment must have its full service kitchen approved by the health department, community development and the fire marshal where state law requires the establishment to be inspected by the fire marshal.
Farm winery shall have the same meaning as set forth and further defined in O.C.G.A. § 3-6-21.1, as may be amended from time to time.
Fortified wine means any alcoholic beverage containing more than 21 percent alcohol by volume made from fruits, berries, or grapes, either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. Fortified wine includes, but is not limited to, brandy.
Full service kitchen means a kitchen that must contain at least a three-compartment pot sink, a commercial grade stove or grill and oven which is permanently installed, and a commercial grade cooler or refrigerator. The full service kitchen must be approved by the health department, community development, and the fire marshal, where State law requires the establishment to be inspected by the fire marshal.
Georgia farm winery shall have the same meaning as set forth and further defined in O.C.G.A. § 3-6-21.1, as may be amended from time to time.
Golf course means a 70, 71, or 72 par course and being a recognized member of the Georgia State Golf Association and United States Golf Association. Consisting of a track of land not less than 90 acres in size dedicated for playing the game of golf. An eighteen-hole course shall not measure less than 6,000 yards from the men's tees as governed by the United States Golf Association.
Golf course premises means the golf course, club house, driving range, swimming pool, patios, open areas, and other recreational areas located on or immediately adjoining the golf course. The term shall not include, however, the parking lots, county roads or rights-of-way, or other areas commonly used by private motor vehicles.
Individual means a natural person.
License means a license for the sale of alcoholic beverages issued pursuant to the terms of this chapter.
Licensee means any person who holds a permit from the board of commissioners to sell alcoholic beverages.
Off-premises consumption means the sale of alcoholic beverages at retail, only to consumers and not for resale, in unbroken packages for consumption off the licensed premises.
On-premises consumption means the sale of alcoholic beverages by the drink or in broken packages at retail, for consumption on the licensed premises.
Package means a bottle, can, or other original consumer container.
Person means any individual, firm, partnership, cooperative, nonprofit membership corporation, joint venture, association, company, corporation, agency, syndicate, estate, trust, business trust, receiver, fiduciary, or other group or combination acting as a unit, body politic, or political subdivision, whether public, private, or quasi-public.
Premises means a physically identifiable place of business of one or more contiguous rooms, operating under the same trade name, where alcoholic beverages are sold. In hotels and private clubs, the premises shall include eating areas, ballrooms, meeting facilities, reception rooms, guest rooms and patio areas of such hotel or private club located within the boundaries of the land on which such hotel or private club is built.
Private club means any nonprofit association organized under the law of the State of Georgia which:
(a) Has been in existence for at least one year prior to filing an application for a license to be issued pursuant to this chapter:
(b) Has at least 75 regular dues-paying members: and
(c) Owns, hires, or leases a building or space within a building for reasonable use of its members, which building space:
1. Has full service kitchen and dining room space and equipment;
2. Is staffed with a sufficient number of employees for cooking, preparing and serving meals for its members and guests; and
3. Has no member, officer, agent or employee directly or indirectly receiving, in the form a salary or other compensation, any profits from the sale of alcoholic beverages beyond a "fixed salary" as such term is defined in O.C.G.A. § 3-7-1, as may be amended from time to time.
Retailer or retail dealer means, except as to distilled spirits, any person who sells alcoholic beverages, either in unbroken packages or for consumption on the premises, at retail only to consumers and not for re-sale.
Sample means a tasting of an individual wine in an amount of not more than two ounces, which may be given as complimentary or for a fee not to exceed more than four samples in a 24-hour period.
Tasting room shall have the same meaning as set forth and further defined in O.C.G.A. § 3-6-21.1, as may be amended from time to time.
Wholesaler means any person who sells alcoholic beverages to other wholesale dealers, to off-premises and on-premises consumption licensee.
Wine means any alcoholic beverage made from fruits, berries or grapes which contains not more than 21 percent alcohol, either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. This term includes, but is not limited to, all sparkling wines, champagnes, combinations of such beverages, vermouths, special natural wines, sake, rectified wines, etc. This term does not include cooking wine mixed with salt or other ingredients so as to render it unfit for human consumption as a beverage. A liquid shall first be deemed to be a wine at the point in the manufacturing process when it conforms to this definition.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025; Ord. of 12-11-2025)
127:
(a) Alcoholic beverages may only be sold in the unincorporated area of the county under a license granted by the board of commissioners, upon the terms and conditions provided in this chapter.
(b) All licenses issued under the terms of this chapter shall be a grant of privilege to carry on the business of selling alcoholic beverages during the term of the license, subject to all terms and conditions imposed by the terms of the license and the laws of the county and the state.
(c) All licenses issued under the terms of this chapter shall have printed on the front of such licenses the following words: "This license is a mere privilege subject to be revoked and annulled and is subject to any further ordinances which may be enacted by the Board of Commissioners of Lincoln County, Georgia."
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
128:
It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in any of the following activities:
(a) To drink, serve or offer for drinking or have possession for sale or distribution, any type of alcoholic beverage in any county park, playground or building without an appropriate alcoholic beverage license and occupational tax license.
(b) To sell or offer for sale or serve for remuneration whether the payment is direct or indirect, any alcoholic beverage at retail or wholesale without the appropriate alcoholic beverage license and occupational tax license.
(c) To engage in any act involving the sale, service or consumption of alcoholic beverages prohibited by laws of the state.
(d) To violate any of the provisions of this chapter.
(e) To permit any person to engage in any activity on the premises for which the license is issued or within the place of business, which is in violation of the laws or regulations of any federal, state, county, municipal governing authority or regulatory agency. With respect to any such activity, it shall be presumed that the same was done with the knowledge or consent of the licensee, provided however, that such presumption may be rebutted only by evidence which precludes every other reasonable hypothesis save that the licensee did not know, assist or aid in such occurrence, or in the exercise of full diligence could not have discovered or prevented such activity.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
129:
The penalties for any violation of this chapter, unless otherwise specified in this chapter, shall be as follows:
(a) For any violation of this chapter, such penalties and costs as set forth in section 1-9; and
(b) In addition to the penalties set forth in subsection (a) of this section and totally distinct and separate from such penalties, any violation of this chapter or any failure to comply with the requirements of this chapter shall be grounds for immediate suspension or revocation of any or all licenses issued under this chapter held by the licensee, regardless of the number of licenses or locations involved and regardless of whether or not the licensee knew of or contributed to such violation. It is the intent of this subsection, without limiting its generality, to grant the board of commissioners the right to suspend or revoke any and all licenses held by a licensee when any violation of this chapter occurs at any place of business operated by the licensee pursuant to a license issued under this chapter.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
130:
All licenses issued by the board of commissioners for the sale of alcoholic beverages which are outstanding on September 11, 2025, the effective date of this chapter, shall continue in effect until they expire according to the terms of such licenses. Upon the expiration of such licenses, renewal licenses must be obtained pursuant to the terms of this chapter.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
131:
All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict with this chapter are expressly repealed.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
132:
If the board of commissioners deems it necessary to conduct an audit of the records and books of the licensee, the board of commissioners shall notify the licensee of the date, time, and place of the audit. The board of commissioners may designate the county's auditor or other designated person to perform any audit authorized in this chapter. Licensees shall cooperate with the audit or forfeit any license issued pursuant to this chapter.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
133:
(a) No licensee shall purchase alcoholic beverages from any person other than a wholesaler licensed under this chapter or by the state. No wholesaler shall sell any alcoholic beverage to anyone other than a retailer licensed under this chapter; provided, however, that this section shall not prohibit the purchase by one retailer of another retailer's entire stock in a bona fide purchase of an ongoing business.
(b) No alcoholic beverages shall be delivered to any licensee in the county except by a wholesaler. The name of the wholesaler shall be clearly marked on the delivery vehicle.
(c) The board of commissioners may request, from time to time, information concerning purchases and sales of alcoholic beverages from retailers and wholesalers.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
134:
All facilities for which a license shall be issued shall have adequate sanitary toilet facilities and shall be adequately illuminated so that all hallways, passageways and open areas may be clearly seen by the customers in such facility. The licensee shall maintain the premises, the building in which the license premises is located, the surrounding grounds, and parking areas in a neat, clean and well maintained condition and appearance, free of trash, litter and any unsightly conditions at all times.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
135:
(a) The sale of alcoholic beverages shall be lawful during the polling hours of any election; however, nothing herein shall authorize the sale of alcoholic beverages within 250 feet of a polling place during such time as the polls are opened.
(b) Notwithstanding the foregoing, no alcoholic beverages of any kind shall be sold during any day or part of the day when the sale of said alcoholic beverage is prohibited by state law.
(c) Alcoholic beverages may be sold at all times, not otherwise prohibited by state law.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
136:
No person while holding any license shall require, permit, suffer, encourage, or induce any employee or person other than the patron and guests of the patron, to solicit the purchase by the patron of any drink, whether alcoholic or non-alcoholic, or money with which to purchase the same; nor shall any licensee pay a commission or any other compensation to any person frequenting his establishment or to his agent or manager to solicit for herself, himself, or for others, the purchase by the patron of any drink, whether alcoholic or non-alcoholic.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
137:
It shall be unlawful for any person to add to the contents of any bottle labeled as containing an alcoholic beverage, or to refill any such empty bottle, or in any manner to misrepresent the quantity, quality or brand name of any alcoholic beverage.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
138:
Gambling, betting, or the operation of games of chance, punchboards, slot machines, lotteries, or tickets or chances therein, or any other such scheme or device involving the hazarding of money or any other thing of value in any licensed place of business, or in any room adjoining the same owned, leased or controlled by him, shall be cause for suspension or revocation of his license; provided, however, nothing herein shall prohibit the operation of a properly licensed state lottery outlet, bingo game or any device not otherwise prohibited by law.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
139:
(a) It shall be the duty of the licensee of the premises licensed under this article to maintain a copy of this chapter, or the ordinance from which this chapter derives, and all amendments thereto, on such premises, and to instruct each and every employee on the terms thereof.
(b) No person shall be approved for a license hereunder, unless such person shall have read the county alcoholic beverage regulations in full text, and shall certify in writing the fact of such reading and the knowledge thereof.
(c) No person shall be approved for employment by a licensee, unless such person shall have read the county alcoholic beverage regulations in full text, and shall certify in writing the fact of such reading and the knowledge thereof.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
140:
All premises for which an alcoholic beverage license has been issued under the provisions of this chapter shall be adequately illuminated so that all hallways, passageways and open areas may be clearly seen by customers therein.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
141:
(a) No sign or advertisement of alcoholic beverages shall be erected or installed outside the place of business or at any outside location advertising for the sale of alcoholic beverages or offering for sale alcoholic beverages generally or at any other location or establishment.
(b) Lighted signs advertising alcoholic beverages must be turned off when the business is closed, or any day in which the sale of alcoholic beverages is prohibited.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
142:
No screen, blind, curtain, partition, article, or thing shall be permitted in the window or upon the doors of the licensed premises which shall prevent a clear view into the interior of the premises from the street or road at any time, and no booth, screen, partition or other obstruction shall be permitted within the interior of the licensed premises, and the same shall be so lighted so the interior of the premises is plainly visible from the street or road day or night.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
143:
No licensee, or his business associates, shall borrow or accept from or give or lend to vending machine owners, lessors, suppliers or operators, money or other valuable considerations. Vending machines shall mean coin-in-slot devices dispensing goods, services, or amusements, or any other thing of value.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
144:
(a) Alcoholic beverage sales can be made by an on-premises consumption licensee in a patio/open area type environment on the premises if the on-premises consumption licensee has been approved to do so by the board of commissioners.
(b) To obtain such approval, the patio/open area must be enclosed by a permanent structure providing for public ingress/egress only through the main structure on the premises covered by the license.
(c) The height of the enclosing structure shall be a minimum of 42 inches above ground level. Such enclosing structure does not have to be solid, nor does it have to restrict visibility into or out of the patio/open sales area. Such enclosing structure must be permitted and approved by the director of community development.
(d) There must be an approved emergency fire exit (not for general public use unless an emergency exists) from the patio/open sales area which should be of the type that sounds an alarm so that the licensee will be alerted in the event of unauthorized use when no emergency exists.
(e) If a licensee desires a patio/open sales area inside an existing structure, plans will be reviewed and approved on an individual basis by the board of commissioners after consultation with the director of community development. Interior-type patio/open sales areas must also meet the requirements of the county's planning, zoning, engineering and fire codes, and any applicable codes of the state.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
145:
(a) It is prohibited for customers to leave the premises with open alcoholic beverages, and it is the licensee's responsibility to ensure that no open beverages are sold and carried out.
(b) It is prohibited for customers to gather outside any alcoholic beverage establishment and consume alcoholic beverages.
(c) It is prohibited for any manager or any employee to allow persons to gather outside any alcoholic beverage establishment and consume alcoholic beverages.
(d) It shall be unlawful for any person to consume any alcoholic beverages while in the confines of any motor vehicle when the vehicle is parked in the parking lot of any alcoholic beverage establishment.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
146:
(a) No individual shall be allowed to consume alcoholic beverages in any restaurant with an occupation tax certificate from the county that does not have a license for on-premises consumption of alcoholic beverages under this chapter.
(b) The occupation tax licensee for any restaurant in the county shall not allow any individual to consume alcoholic beverages on their premises that were not purchased from the restaurant.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
147:
Noise levels above those otherwise allowed by county ordinances shall not be permitted beyond the boundaries of the land on which facilities operated pursuant to a license under this article are located.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
148:
If any section, provision, or clause of any part of this chapter shall be declared invalid or unconstitutional, or if the provisions of any part of this chapter as applied to any particular situation or set of circumstances shall be declared invalid or unconstitutional, such [invalidity] shall not be construed to affect the portions of this chapter not so held to be invalid, or the application of this chapter to other circumstances not so held to be invalid. It is hereby declared as the intent that this chapter would have been adopted had such invalid portion not been included herein.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
151:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to sell or process for the purpose of sale any alcoholic beverage in the county, excluding the City of Lincolnton, when such person is not operating pursuant to a license granted by the board of commissioners.
(b) Licenses granted hereunder shall fall into one or more of the following classes:
(1) Class A: Off-premises consumption of beer and wine.
(2) Class B: On-premises consumption of beer and wine.
(3) Class C: On-premises consumption of liquor, includes beer and wine.
(4) Class D: Sale and distribution of beer and wine at wholesale.
(5) Class E: Manufacturing beer and wine.
(6) Class F: Tasting room and farm winery.
(7) Class G: Brew pubs.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025; Ord. of 12-11-2025)
152:
(a) Upon making an application for a license under this article, the applicant shall pay a license fee for the license, an administrative and investigative fee, and any such other fees as may be established from time to time by the board of commissioners by resolution adopted in open meeting and kept on file in the office of the county clerk. All applicants shall be furnished with a copy of the schedule of fees at the time of application for a license under this article.
(b) All fees and taxes due to the state and/or county by the applicant, or the property on which the establishment is to be located, must be paid in full at or prior to the time of the filing of the application for license.
(c) All licenses granted under this article shall be for a calendar year or the balance thereof. The full license fee shall be paid for a license issued on or after January 1, but prior to July 1 of such year. One-half of the license fee shall be paid if the license is issued on or after July 1 of the calendar year for which the license is issued. The license fee for temporary permits under section 10-150 shall not be adjusted in any case.
(d) If the application is denied or if the applicant withdraws its application prior to the hearing by the board of commissioners, the license fee will be refunded, however the administrative and investigation fees are non-refundable.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
153:
Each license under this article shall be limited to the operation of an establishment or enterprise for the sale of alcoholic beverages at a specific location as set forth in the license. Separate applications must be made, separate fees, and separate licenses must be obtained for each location at which an activity requiring a license is conducted.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
154:
(a) Locations.
(1) Eating establishments. For an eating establishment to be eligible to sell alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises, it must be a public place, kept, used, maintained, advertised and held out to sell prepared food for consumption on the premises to the general public, with a full service kitchen offering food service every hour such establishment is open and dining room equipped and having a seating capacity of at least 40 people. The serving of such meals shall be the principal business conducted, with the serving of distilled spirits to be consumed on the premises as only incidental thereto, and to qualify as an eating establishment under this section, such establishment must derive at least 50 percent of its total annual gross food and beverage sales from the sales of prepared meals and foods. Upon receiving an application from an eating establishment to sell alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises, the director of community development shall inspect the restaurant to determine if the applicant is in compliance with the requirements for a restaurant in this article and shall advise the board of commissioners the determination of his inspection.
(2) Golf course premises as defined in section 10-2.
(3) Bona fide private club as defined in section 10-2.
(b) Upon renewal of an alcoholic beverage license at a premises where an eating establishment, golf course, or bona fide private club is in operation the director of community development shall verify the sales requirements in this section. Failure of a licensee to cooperate in the verification of sales shall be a violation of this article.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025; Ord. of 12-11-2025)
155:
(a) A person desiring to obtain a license under this article shall make application to the director of community development on the forms prescribed by the board of commissioners.
(b) The application shall include, but not be limited to, confirmation that all criteria required under this article has been satisfied.
(c) All applicants shall furnish the account number of the current occupation tax for that location, certification from the county tax commissioner that all taxes due to the county by the applicant have been paid and other material as required by the director of community development. Failure to furnish such data as required by the director of community development shall be deemed to be a withdrawal of the application.
(d) Each application for an initial license shall include a plat of the land on which the establishment is proposed to be located showing the location of the improvements thereon. The plat must be prepared by a land surveyor registered under the laws of the state and the surveyor shall show on the plat, and certify as to the accuracy thereof, the distance from the main entrance door of the proposed establishment to any school building, church building, county park or playground, alcoholic treatment facility measured under the applicable provisions of section 10-59.
(e) All applications shall be sworn to by the applicant before a notary public or other officer empowered by law to administer oaths.
(f) The director of community development shall review all applications, make all necessary inspections and/or investigations, and may request oral interrogation of any person or persons involved in any transaction pertinent to the application or any evidence relevant to the application, as they deem necessary to complete the application review process.
(g) Failure of the applicant to comply with subsection (f) of this section within 30 days, shall result in the automatic dismissal of the application.
(h) An application shall be presented to the board of commissioners within 45 days after the date such application is deemed complete by the director of community development. The director shall notify the applicant in writing of the date on which the application will be presented to the board of commissioners, which notice shall be given in sufficient time to enable the applicant to meet the public notice requirements as set forth in section 10-58.
(i) At the time the application is presented to the board of commissioners the applicant shall appear and present any matters in support of the application and any other person may appear and present matters in opposition to the application. Upon hearing all of the presentations, the board of commissioners shall take action denying or granting the application or deferring action for a period not to exceed 45 days in order to obtain further information. If the application is denied, the board of commissioners shall set forth the reasons for the denial in writing.
(j) In all instances in which an application is denied under the provisions of this article, the applicant, or related person or entity, may not reapply for a similar license for the same location for at least one year from the date of such denial.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
156:
Agents and inspectors appointed by the county commission for the enforcement of this chapter, including officers of the county sheriff's office, are empowered and authorized to enter upon the premises of any person or entity engaged in the manufacture, sale, distribution, storage, or transportation of alcoholic beverages and distilled spirits at any time for the purpose of inspecting said premises and shall have access during such inspection to all books, records, and supplies relating to the manufacture, sale distribution, storage, and transportation of alcoholic beverages and distilled spirits.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
157:
Any application for a license made pursuant to this article may be withdrawn by the applicant at any time. If the application is withdrawn before the license is issued, any sums deposited as license fees will be refunded. After issuance of a license, no refunds will be made. No refunds shall be made under any circumstances for investigation and administrative fees required in this article.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
158:
(a) Citizenship; residency. A license will be issued only to a person who is a citizen of the United States or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence in the United States. Where an applicant is other than a natural person, it must be an entity organized and existing under the laws of the United States or one of its states, an agent of the entity must meet the qualifications set forth herein.
(1) Where the applicant for a license is an entity other than a natural person, the application shall be made jointly in the name of the entity and an officer having authority to bind the entity. Said entity shall be registered to do business in the State of Georgia.
(2) Licenses issued to entities must be issued jointly to the entity and all of the other persons required by this section to join in the application. All respective partners, officers, directors, or members, as applicable, shall be responsible for the actions of the named licensee and the conduct of the licensed business.
(b) Operation of business. If none of the applicants required above have primary responsibility of the day to day operations of the business for which the license is sought, then the operating manager shall join in the application. All persons named on the application shall be deemed "applicants".
(c) Background check. The person who has the primary responsibilities of the day to day operations of the business for which the license is sought shall submit a personnel statement in the form prescribed by the board of commissioners and submit to a fingerprint background check.
(d) Moral character; criminal record. No person or entity shall be granted an alcoholic beverage license unless it shall appear to the satisfaction of the board of commissioners that such persons or partners in the firms or officers and directors of the company shall be of good moral character.
(e) Age. An applicant must be 21 years of age or older.
(f) Interest in business; involvement in business. An applicant must have a bona-fide interest in the business for which the license is sought.
(g) Eligibility. The following individuals are not eligible for an alcoholic beverage license, even if they possess all of the qualifications listed herein.
(1) Any person convicted of a felony within the ten years immediately preceding the date of receipt of submission of the application.
(2) Any person convicted of a misdemeanor within the five years immediately preceding the date of receipt of submission of the application.
(3) Any person who has been convicted of a crime of moral turpitude or gambling within ten years immediately preceding the date of receipt of submission of the application.
(4) Any person whose license to sell alcoholic beverages has been revoked for cause in any county, municipality, state or territory of the United States within the ten years preceding the filing of the application.
(5) Any person who has knowingly falsified information or made any material misrepresentation on the application for a license under this chapter or any application under the predecessor ordinance for Lincoln County submitted within the ten years preceding the filing of the application.
(6) Any person who has been convicted of a violation of any federal, state or local law pertaining to the possession, manufacture, or sale of alcoholic beverages, controlled substances, or imitation controlled substances within the ten years preceding the filing of the application.
(7) Should any such applicant, partner or officer or director of any applicant entity, after a license has been granted, be convicted or plead guilty or nolo contendere to a crime involving moral turpitude, or to the violation of any laws of the State of Georgia regulating possession or the sale of controlled substances, imitation controlled substances, drugs, liquors, wine or beer or the lottery laws of this state, said license shall be subject after hearing to immediate suspension or revocation. Should the operating manager be convicted or plead guilty or nolo contendere to a crime involving moral turpitude, or to the violation of any laws of the State of Georgia regulating possession or the sale of narcotics, drugs, liquors, wine or beer or the lottery laws of this state, the licensee shall have seven days to report to the director of community development any such violation, and 45 days from such conviction to revise its license to add a new operating manager. Failure to report a violation within the time prescribed shall automatically revoke applicant's license.
(h) Surrogates. The board of commissioners may decline to issue a license under this article when any person having any ownership interest in or any control over the land or building in which the establishment to be operated pursuant to the license will be located, or where any person who has control over the operation of the establishment, does not meet the same character requirements as set forth in this section for the licensee.
(i) Registered agent. Applicant must appoint and continuously maintain in the county a registered agent upon whom any process, notice or demand required or permitted by law or under this article may be served. The registered agent must be a resident of Lincoln County. The licensee shall file the name of such registered agent, along with the written consent to serve of such agent, with the director of community development.
(j) Extenuating circumstances. The board of commissioners, in its discretion, may consider any extenuating circumstances which may reflect favorably or unfavorably on the applicant, the application or the proposed location of the establishment. If, in the board of commissioners' judgment, circumstances are such that issuing of a license under this article would not be in the best interest of the general public, such circumstances may be grounds for denying the application.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
159:
A person filing an application for a new license under this article as opposed to an application for the renewal of an existing license shall give public notice of the filing of the application as follows:
(a) By publishing a notice of the application in the newspaper in which sheriff's sales in the county are placed, in a form approved by the board of commissioners, three times in the 30 days preceding the consideration of the application by the board of commissioners;
(b) By posting a sign for at least 30 days preceding the consideration of the application by the board of commissioners in a prominent position on the property where it can be readily read from the road, which states:
" This establishment has applied to the Lincoln County Commission for an alcoholic beverage license authorizing it to sell (beer) (wine) (distilled spirits) for consumption (on) (off) premise at this location. This ___ day of ___, 20___.
Name of Applicant:_______
Address of Applicant:_______."
(c) Any location which has never been licensed for the sale of alcoholic beverages before, or for which a license has been revoked, or where the sale of alcohol has ceased for nine months, shall be considered a new location.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
160:
No person knowingly and intentionally may sell or offer to sell:
(a) Any distilled spirits in or within:
(1) Three hundred feet of any church or church building; or
(2) Six hundred feet of any school building, county park or playground.
(b) Any beer or wine in or within 300 feet of any church building, school building, county park or playground.
(c) Alcoholic beverages, of any kind, within 300 feet of an alcoholic treatment center owned and operated by this state or any county or municipal government therein.
(d) For purposes of this section, subject to the qualifications set forth in this subsection, distances shall be measured in a straight line from the main entrance door of the establishment for which the license under this article is being sought to the nearest point on the boundary line of the land making up the campus of the church building, school building, county park or playground, or alcoholic treatment facility.
(e) No establishment which is being operated pursuant to a county license to sell alcohol on September 11, 2025, the effective date of this article, shall be denied continued operation under such existing license, nor denied any renewal of such license, be denied a new license based upon the measurements set forth in this section. Upon cessation of the operation of the establishment such exemption shall cease. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the cessation of the operation of the establishment is for one year or less, such exemption shall not cease.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
161:
A license issued under this article shall at all times be kept plainly exposed to public view at the place of business for which the license was granted.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
162:
(a) No license issued under this article shall be transferable, except as otherwise provided in this section.
(b) In case of the death of a licensee who is the sole licensee, the establishment for which the license was issued shall be allowed to continue to sell alcoholic beverages in accordance with the terms of the license for a period of 45 days from the date of death of the licensee or until approval of a new licensee, whichever shall first occur; provided, however, that no sale of alcoholic beverages shall be allowed after the seventh day after the date of death of the licensee until such time as a personal representative of the estate of the deceased licensee, appointed by a probate court of competent jurisdiction, shall have registered with the director of community development on forms approved by the board of commissioners. Such personal representative shall be subject to all of the requirements that applied to the deceased licensee and shall agree in writing to operate the establishment during the interim period in accordance with the terms of the license and the laws of the state and county.
(c) In the case of licenses issued jointly to an entity, if there is a change in control or ownership of the licensee, partnership, corporation or other business entity, then an application for a new license must be filed within seven days. Upon issuance of a new license, the authorization to sell under the previous license shall be revoked by operation of law. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the only change in control of the licensee, partnership, corporation or other business entity is a change in the operating manager, a new license shall not be required. A licensee shall have 45 days to hire a new operating manager, and the new operating manager shall, within seven days of being hired, submit a personnel statement in the form prescribed by the board of commissioners, and submit to a fingerprint background check.
(d) If there is a change in control or ownership of licensee's entity, and if an application for a new license is filed with the director of community development within seven days of such sale or transfer, the establishment may continue to be operated under the then existing license for a period of 45 days or until a new license is issued or denied, whichever shall occur first.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
163:
(a) A license shall automatically terminate without further action in the event that any licensee, for a period of two consecutive months after the license under this article has been issued, ceases to operate the business of selling alcoholic beverages as authorized in the license.
(b) If the business operation of selling alcoholic beverages is interrupted as a result of damage to the premises which is being repaired or because the premises are being remodeled, then this section shall not apply to such cessation of operation.
(c) If a license is issued for the operation of an establishment in a building which has not yet been completed, the license will not be forfeited unless the licensee fails to begin operations within a period of the earlier of 60 days after a certificate of occupancy is awarded or 180 days from the date of issuance of the license.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
164:
(a) All licenses granted under this article shall expire on December 31 of each year and licensees who desire to renew their license shall file a renewal application with the director of community development on forms provided for such renewal of the license for the ensuing year.
(b) Applications for renewal must be filed on or before October 31 of each year. If a renewal application is received after October 31, the county cannot assure the applicant that a renewal license will be issued by January 1 and the licensee will have to cease the sale of alcoholic beverages from January 1 until the renewal license is issued.
(c) If a license renewal application is received after December 31, such application shall be treated as an application for a new license and the applicant shall be required to comply with all rules, regulations and fees for the granting of licenses as if no previous license had been issued.
(d) Any person applying for renewal of a license must pay the license, administrative and investigative fees at the time of filing the application. Failure to pay such fees at that time shall result in the application for renewal being treated as not filed or withdrawn.
(e) Any person applying for a renewal license who meets the qualifications of section 10-57 shall be issued a renewed license.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
167:
(a) License required. A brewer license is required before a manufacturer will be allowed to manufacture malt beverages within the boundaries of the county, except that a brewpub is not required to obtain a brewer license but must obtain a brewpub license.
(b) On-premises consumption. In the event a brewer license holder exercises its right to sell malt beverages for on-premises consumption, said manufacturer shall first obtain a retail consumption license.
(c) Sales to individuals. A brewer license holder may sell malt beverages to individuals, provided, however, that such sales are limited to 2,000 barrels of malt beverages per year produced at the manufacturer's licensed premises to the following individuals:
(1) Those who are on such premises for the consumption of the malt beverages on the licensed premises; and
(2) Those who will consume the malt beverages off the licensed premises, provided, however, that such sales shall not exceed a maximum of 288 ounces of malt beverages per consumer per day.
(d) Free samples. A brewer license holder is allowed to offer or permit free sampling of malt beverages, but only in accordance with the laws of this state.
(e) Excise tax. A brewer license holder who sells malt beverages to individuals for off-premises consumption shall be subject to the provisions herein of article III, section 10-127. A brewer license holder who sells malt beverages to individuals for on-premises consumption shall also be subject to the provisions herein of the same section. The director of community development may request from time to time information concerning purchases and sales of alcoholic beverages from the brewer license holder.
(f) A brewer may sell malt beverages on all days and at all times that the sales of malt beverages by retailers are lawful within the county and the state.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
168:
(a) Required. No individual shall be permitted to own or operate a brewpub without first obtaining a proper license and each brewpub license holder shall comply with all other applicable state and local license requirements.
(b) Terms of license.
(1) A brewpub license authorizes the holder of such license to:
a. Manufacture on the licensed premises not more than 2,000 barrels of beer in a calendar year solely for retail sale on the premises and solely in draft form; and
b. Operate an eating establishment that shall be the sole retail outlet for such beer and may offer for sale any other alcoholic beverages produced by other manufacturers which are authorized for retail sale under licenses issued by the board of commissioners, including wine, distilled spirits, and malt beverages, provided that such alcoholic beverages are purchased from a licensed wholesaler for consumption on the premises only, and provided further, that in addition to draft beer manufactured on the premises, each brewpub licensee shall offer for sale commercially available canned or bottled malt beverages from licensed wholesalers.
(2) Possession of a brewpub license shall not prevent the holder of such license from obtaining a retail consumption dealer's license for the same premises.
(3) A brewpub license does not authorize the holder of such license to sell alcoholic beverages by the package for consumption off the premises.
(4) A brewpub licensee shall not offer or permit any free sampling of beer by its customers on the premises of the brewpub.
(5) A brewpub licensee shall:
a. Pay all state and local license fees and excise taxes applicable to individuals licensed as manufacturers, retailers, and where applicable, wholesalers under this chapter; and
b. Measure beer manufactured on the premises and otherwise comply with applicable regulations respecting excise and enforcement tax determination for such beer as required by Georgia law and the ordinances of the Lincoln County, Georgia.
(6) A brewpub may sell malt beverages on all days and at all times the sales of alcoholic beverages by retailers are lawful within the county and the state.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
169:
(a) Farm wineries shall be located on property that has been approved for a conditional use as a farm winery by the board of commissioners of Lincoln County, Georgia under Chapter 34, Land Development Ordinances of the Code of Lincoln County, Georgia.
(b) The farm winery or tasting room shall be located on premises, a substantial portion of which is used for agricultural purposes, including growing the berries, grapes, or fruits to be utilized in the manufacture or production of wine by the winery; or
(c) The farm winery shall be owned and operated by persons who are engaged in the production of a substantial portion of the agricultural produce used in its annual production. The cultivation and growing of the produce for the farm winery shall be located on a parcel of land of not less than five acres.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
170:
Tasting rooms shall be lawful in the unincorporated areas of the county and shall be governed by the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 3-6-21.1, et seq. and this chapter. For purposes of this section, the term "licensed premises" shall mean any location approved by the laws of this state. The operators of farm winery must begin preparing the land for planting and wine production within one year of the beginning of any sales of farm winery products. Thereafter, there must be an active ongoing operation occurring on said property at all times. No residence may be located on the same property as the tasting room.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
171:
(a) Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 3-6-21.3, as may be amended from time to time, the farm winery and tasting room may sell distilled spirits, malt beverages, and wines produced with the approval of the commissioner.
(b) A farm winery shall obtain and have a separate license as set forth in this chapter prior to selling its own wine or wine produced by another Georgia farm winery or through its tasting room.
(c) The qualifications for the license for the sale by a farm winery tasting room shall be the same as set forth in this chapter.
(d) All buildings shall be subject to commercial development standards as set forth in the Lincoln County, Georgia Ordinances and the Lincoln County, Georgia Development Regulations.
(e) The license created in accordance with this chapter shall be limited to farm wineries and tasting rooms licensed by the state in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 3-6-21.1, et. seq. No license is hereby created authorizing any other use.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
173:
(a) A license under this article may be suspended or revoked by the board of commissioners when the licensee furnishes fraudulent or untruthful information on the application or any renewal application for a license, or for failure of the licensee to pay all fees, taxes or other charges imposed under the provisions of this chapter or other laws or ordinances of the county or state.
(b) Whenever the state shall revoke or suspend any permit or license to sell alcoholic beverages, the license issued under this article shall be automatically revoked or suspended, as the case may be.
(c) If the board of commissioners believes that probable cause exists to find that a violation of sections 10-4, 10-12, 10-16, and 10-153 has occurred in an establishment operated pursuant to a license under this article, the board of commissioners may temporarily suspend such license pending final determination and action on the matter by the board of commissioners.
(d) The board of commissioners shall revoke a license under this article where alcoholic beverages have been sold or distributed at the location covered by the license during a period of suspension of such license.
(e) The board of commissioners may suspend or revoke any license under this article when the licensee does not meet the licensing qualifications set forth in this article and such information becomes known to the director of development services or the board of commissioners.
(f) An act or omission of a licensee, its partners, officers, members which constitutes a violation of federal or state law or this chapter will subject the licensee to suspension or revocation of his license when the board of commissioners determines that the act or omission did occur, regardless of whether any criminal prosecution or conviction ensues.
(g) An act or omission of an employee of a licensee on the licensed premises which constitutes a violation of federal or state law or this chapter will subject the licensee to suspension or revocation of his license when the board of commissioners determines that the act or omission did occur, regardless of whether any criminal prosecution or conviction ensues; provided the board of commissioners determines that the acts of the employee were known to or, under reasonable circumstances, should have been known to the licensee, or were condoned by the licensee, or that the licensee had not established reasonable practices or procedures to prevent such act or omission from occurring.
(h) A license issued under this article may be suspended or revoked whenever the board of commissioners determines that a licensee no longer maintains the responsibility upon which issuance of the license was based or whenever the licensee has defaulted in any obligation of any kind whatsoever lawfully owing to the county.
(i) A license issued under this article may be suspended or revoked whenever the board of commissioners determines that the establishment operated pursuant to the license has been the scene of repeated incidents of violence resulting in injury to a person or damage to property or a disturbance of the peace or requiring the intervention of law enforcement officers on the scene of a single incident of severe violence resulting in the death of a person or serious injury to a person requiring inpatient hospital care for the injured person.
(j) Upon completion of any period of suspension, a license under this article shall not be reinstated until the licensee has paid the county a reinstatement fee equal to the original license fee for that calendar year. In addition, the licensee shall pay the administrative and investigative fees and update all license application forms.
(k) A license issued under this article shall be immediately revoked upon a conviction of applicant or any other person required to be named on the application of a violation of any federal, state or local law pertaining to the possession, manufacture, sale or use of alcoholic beverages, controlled substances, or imitation controlled substances.
(l) A license issued under this article shall be revocable for a criminal charge of any violation of federal, state or local law pertaining to the possession, manufacture, sale or use of alcoholic beverages, controlled substances, or imitation controlled substances which took place at the business establishment for which the license is given.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
174:
(a) Unless otherwise provided in this chapter, or unless waived by the licensee, no license under this article shall be suspended or revoked without the opportunity for a hearing as provided in this section.
(b) The director of community development shall provide written notice to the licensee of the initiation of an action to suspend or revoke a license. Such written notification shall set forth, in reasonable detail, the reasons for such action and shall notify the licensee of the right to a hearing under the provisions of this section. Any licensee against whom action for the suspension or revocation of a license is initiated may have a hearing concerning such action before the board of commissioners. Such hearing shall be by written request, filed with the director of community development within seven days after the date of the notice of the initiation of the action from the director to the licensee. Such written request shall set forth the reasons why the licensee feels that the proposed action should not be taken and, in reasonable detail, the grounds and facts which the licensee contends support the licensee's position. The board of commissioners shall determine whether or not the license shall be temporarily suspended during the period prior to the hearing and until action is taken by the board of commissioners. Failure of the licensee to request a hearing within the time specified in this section shall be deemed to be a waiver by the licensee of a right to a hearing, and the board of commissioners shall be authorized to proceed with final action on the matter without the holding of a hearing.
(c) A hearing by the board of commissioners, if requested, shall be held within 21 days of the date of filing the request for a hearing with the director of community development. At such hearing the licensee shall have the right to be represented by an attorney, at the expense of the licensee, and to present evidence and cross-examine witnesses.
(d) The action of the board of commissioners shall be provided in writing to the licensee within seven days after the conclusion of the hearing, by certified mail, return receipt requested.
(e) The action of the board of commissioners shall be final.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
175:
For the purpose of this chapter, notice shall be deemed to be delivered when such notice is personally served or, if mailed, it must be mailed to the licensee at the license premises address given in the latest application for the license under this article by certified mail, return receipt requested, and shall be deemed delivered on the third day after the date of deposit in the United States mail.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
178:
(a) Every purchaser at retail of distilled spirits by the drink in the county shall pay a tax thereon at the rate of three percent of the retail price or charge for such drink, or at such higher rate as may be permitted by the laws of this state.
(b) Such tax shall not apply in any portion of the county in which an excise tax on the sale of distilled spirits by the drink is being imposed, levied and collected by a municipality.
(c) Such tax shall be collected by the retail consumption dealer, who shall remit such tax to the director of community development on or before the twentieth day of the following calendar month, along with a report of the retail consumption dealer's gross sales derived from the sale of distilled spirits by the drink during the reporting period on forms prescribed by the director.
(d) Credit card sales shall be reported as part of gross sales, and taxes collected on such credit card sales shall be submitted to the county in the same manner as required for cash sales.
(e) Each retail consumption dealer shall be allowed a deduction equal to the rate authorized for deductions from state tax under O.C.G.A. § 48-8-50, as amended from time to time, provided that such tax is not delinquent at the time of payment.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
179:
(a) There is levied an excise tax computed at the rate of $0.22 per liter, including a proportionate amount calculated at the same rate on all fractional parts of a liter, on all sales of distilled spirits and wine in the county by wholesalers to retail consumption dealers and retail package dealers.
(b) Such tax shall be paid to the director of community development by the wholesaler selling such distilled spirits or wine to any retail consumption dealer or retail package dealer on or before the twentieth day of the following calendar month, along with a report of the wholesaler's gross sales of distilled spirits and wine in the county during the reporting period on forms prescribed by the director.
(c) Wine containing less than one-half of one percent alcohol by volume shall not be subject to such tax.
(d) It shall be a violation of this chapter for any wholesaler to sell, ship or deliver, in any manner, any distilled spirits or wine to a retail consumption dealer or retail package dealer without collecting such tax.
(e) It shall be unlawful and a violation of this chapter for any retail consumption dealer or retail package dealer to possess, own, hold, store, display or sell any distilled spirits or wine on which such tax has not been paid.
(f) Each wholesaler shall be paid three percent of the amount of taxes collected as reimbursement for collection of the tax, provided that the tax is paid on or before its due date.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
180:
(a) There is levied an excise tax on all beer sold by wholesalers to retail consumption dealers and retail package dealers in the county at the highest rate allowed by the state, but not less than the following:
(1) Where beer is sold in or from a barrel or bulk container, $6.00 on each container sold containing not more than 15.5 gallons, and a proportionate tax at the same rate on all fractional parts of 15.5 gallons; and
(2) Where beer is sold in bottles, cans or other containers, except barrel or bulk containers, a tax of $0.05 per 12 ounces, and a proportionate rate on all fractional parts of 12 ounces.
(b) Beer which contains less than one-half of one percent alcohol by volume shall not be subject to such tax.
(c) Such tax shall be paid to the director of community development by the wholesaler selling the beer to any retail consumption dealer or retail package dealer on or before the twentieth day of the following calendar month, along with a report of the wholesaler's gross sales of beer in the county during the reporting period on forms prescribed by the director.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
181:
(a) Recomputation of tax; authority to make; basis of recomputation. If the director of community development is not satisfied with the return of the tax or the amount of the tax to be paid to the county by any person, the director may cause an audit of the books and records of the licensee to be performed and may compute and determine the amount required to be paid upon the basis of any information within the director's possession or that may come into the director's possession. One or more deficiency determinations may be made of the amount due for one or more monthly periods. It shall be the duty of each licensee subject to the collection or payment of any of the excise taxes set forth in this article to keep and preserve his records relative to the collection and payment of such taxes for three years.
(b) Interest. The amount of the deficiency determination, exclusive of penalties, shall bear interest at the rate of one percent per month, or fraction thereof, from the twentieth day after the close of the monthly period in which the amount or any portion thereof should have been returned until the date of payment thereof.
(c) Offsetting of overpayments. In making a deficiency determination, the director may offset overpayments for a period against underpayments for another period, penalties and the interest on underpayments.
(d) Penalty for negligence or disregard of rules and regulations. If any part of the deficiency for which a deficiency determination has been made is due to negligence or disregard of rules and regulations, a penalty of 20 percent of the amount of such deficiency shall be added to the tax.
(e) Penalty for fraud or intent to evade. If any part of the deficiency for which a deficiency determination is made is due to fraud or an intent to evade any provision of this article or other authorized rules and regulations, a penalty of 50 percent of the deficiency shall be added to such tax.
(f) Notice of director's determination; service of. The director shall give the licensee written notice of a deficiency determination. The notice may be served personally or by mail. If such service is made by mail, such service shall be made pursuant to section 10-102.
(g) Time within which notice is to be mailed. Except in the case of fraud, intent to evade the provisions of this article or authorized rules and regulations, or failure to make a return, every notice of a deficiency determination shall be mailed within three years after the twentieth day of every month following the monthly period for which the amount is proposed to be determined, or within three years after the return is filed, whichever period should last expire.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
182:
(a) Estimate of gross receipts. If any licensee fails to make a return, the director of community development shall make an estimate of the amount of the gross receipts of the licensee or of the total sales in the county which are subject to the tax. The estimate shall be made for the period in respect to which the licensee failed to make the return and shall be based upon any information which is in or may come into the possession of the director. Upon the basis of such estimate, the director shall compute and determine the amount required to be paid to the county, adding to such determined sum a penalty equal to 15 percent thereof. One or more determinations may be made for one or more periods.
(b) Offsetting of overpayments. If making a determination, the director may offset overpayments for a period or penalties against the interest on the underpayments.
(c) Interest on amount found due. The amount of the determination, exclusive of penalties, shall bear interest at the rate of one percent per month, or fraction thereof, from the twentieth day of the month following the monthly period for which the amount, or any portion thereof, should have been returned, until the date of payment.
(d) Penalty for fraud or intent to evade. If the failure of any person to file a return is due to fraud or an intent to evade the provisions of this article or rules and regulations, a penalty of 25 percent of the amount required to be paid by the person, exclusive of penalties, shall be added thereto in addition to the 20 percent penalty provided in section 10-128.
(e) Giving of notice; manner of service. Promptly after making his determination, the director shall give to the person written notice, to be served personally or by mail in the manner prescribed for service of notice in section 10-102.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
183:
(a) Security. Whenever the director of community development services deems it necessary to ensure compliance with the provisions of this article, he may require any person subject to such sections to deposit with him such security as the director may determine. The amount of the security shall be fixed by the director but shall not be greater than twice the person's estimated average liability for the period for which he files returns, determined in such a manner as the director deems proper, or $10,000.00, whichever amount is the lesser. The amount of the security may be increased by the director subject to the limitations provided in this section. The director may sell the security at public auction, with the approval of the board of commissioners, if it becomes necessary to do so in order to recover any tax or any amount required to be collected, interest or penalty due. Notice of the sale may be served upon the person who deposited the security personally or by mail. If service is by mail, it shall be made in the manner prescribed for service of a notice of determined deficiency and shall be addressed to the person at his address as it appears in the records of the director. Upon any sale, any surplus above the amounts due shall be returned to the person who deposited the security.
(b) Notice of delinquency to persons holding credits or property of delinquent; duty of persons so notified. If any person is delinquent in the payment of the amount required to be paid by him, or if a delinquency determination has been made against him which remains unpaid, the director may, not later than three years after the payment became delinquent, give notice thereof by registered mail to all persons in the county having in their possession or under their control any credits or other personal property belonging to the delinquent, or owing any debts to the delinquent. After receiving the notice, the persons so notified shall neither transfer nor make any other disposition of the credits, other personal property or debts in their possession or under their control at the time they receive the notice until the director consents to a transfer or disposition, or until 20 days elapse after the receipt of the notice. All persons so notified shall, within five days after receipt of the notice, advise the director of all of the credits, other personal property or debts in their possession, under their control or owing by them.
(c) Action for tax collection. At any time within three years after any tax or any amount of tax required to be collected under this article becomes due and payable, and at any time within three years after the delinquency of any tax or any amount of tax required to be collected under this article, the director may bring an action in the courts of this state, any other state or of the United States in the name of county to collect the amount delinquent, together with penalties and interest, court fees, filing fees, attorney's fees and other legal fees incident thereto.
(d) Duty of successors or assignees of licensee to withhold tax from purchase money. If any licensee liable for any amount under the provisions of this article sells out his business or quits the business, his successors or assigns shall withhold a sufficient amount of the purchase price to cover such amount until the former owner produces a receipt from the director showing that he has been paid or a certificate stating that no amount is due.
(e) Liability for failure to withhold; certificate of notice of amount due; time to enforce successor's liability. If the purchaser of a business fails to withhold the purchase price as required, he becomes personally liable for the payment of the amount required to be withheld by him to the extent of the purchase price valued in money. Within 30 days after receiving a written request from the purchaser for a certificate, the director shall either issue the certificate or mail notice to the purchaser at his address, as it appears on the records of the director, of the amount that must be paid as a condition of issuing the certificate. The time within which the obligation of the successor may be enforced shall begin at the time the licensee sells out his business or at the time that the determination against the licensee becomes final, whichever occurs later.
(f) Refund of tax, penalty or interest paid more than once or illegally collected. Whenever the amount of any tax, penalty or interest has been paid more than once, or has been erroneously or illegally collected or received by the county under the provisions of this article it may be offset as provided in subsection 10-128 or it may be refunded provided a verified claim in writing therefor, stating the specific grounds upon which the claim is founded, is filed with the director within three years from the date of payment. The claim shall be audited and shall be made on forms provided by the director. If the claim is approved by the director and the board of commissioners, the excess amount collected or paid may be refunded or may be credited on any amounts then due and payable from the person from whom it was collected or by whom paid, and the balance may be refunded to such person, his administrators or executors.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
184:
The chairman of the board of commissioners shall enforce all requirements within this article.
(a) Authority of the director of community development. The chairman of the board of commissioners, or at his or her direction, the director of community development shall administer and enforce the provisions of this article for the levy and collection of the tax imposed by this article. In the event that there is an alleged violation of this section any member of the board of commissioners or any entity accused of a violation may have the matter brought before the entire board of commissioners.
(b) Rules and regulations. The director of community development shall have the power and authority to make and publish reasonable rules and regulations not inconsistent with this article or other laws of the county and the state, or the constitution of this state or the United States for the administration and enforcement of the provisions of this article and the collection of the taxes hereunder.
(c) Records required for operators, etc.; form. Every licensee for the sale of alcoholic beverages by the drink in this county to a person shall keep such records, receipts, invoices and other pertinent papers in such form as the director of community development may require.
(d) Examination of records; audits. The director of community development, the internal auditor of the county, or any person authorized in writing by the director, may examine the books, paper, records, financial reports, equipment and other facilities of any licensee liable for the tax, in order to verify the accuracy of any return made by the licensee, to ascertain and determine the amount required to be paid.
(e) Authority to require reports; contents. In the administration of the provisions of this article, the director of community development may require the filing of reports by any person or class of persons having in such person's or persons' possession or custody information relating to the sales of alcoholic beverages which are subject to the tax. The reports shall be filed with the director when required by the director and shall set forth the price charged for each sale, the date or dates of sale and such other information as the director of community development may require.
(f) Disclosure of business operators, etc.; limitations on rule. The director of community development or any person having an administrative duty under this article shall not make known in any manner the business affairs, operations or information obtained by an audit of books, papers, records, financial reports, equipment and other facilities of any licensee or any other person visited or examined in the discharge of official duty, or the amount of source income, profits, losses, expenditures or any particular thereof, set forth, or disclosed in any return, or to permit any return or copy thereof or any book containing any abstract or particulars thereof to be seen or examined by any person not having administrative duty under this chapter, except in the case of judicial proceedings or other proceedings necessary to collect the tax hereby levied and assessed. Successors, receivers, trustees, executors, administrators, and assignees, if directly interested, may be given information as to the items included in the measure and the amount of unpaid tax or amounts of tax required to be collected, interest, and penalties.
(Ord. of 9-11-2025)
187:

(a) Any special event, or meeting, occurring at any location within the boundaries of Lincoln County, Georgia, which has been awarded any alcohol license, and serves alcohol at a special event, shall be required to have a minimum of one deputy sheriff (or other security officer approved by the sheriff or his or her designee) on duty and at the location at all times during the special event's hours. Once the number of people at the special event exceeds 75, then one additional deputy sheriff (or other security officer approved by the sheriff or his or her designee) must be present. Once the number of people at the event is above 150, the sheriff of Lincoln County (or his or her designee) shall determine the number of additional deputy sheriffs (or other security officer approved by the sheriff or his or her designee) required at the special event location. If the sheriff (or his or her designee) determines that in order to provide for the safety of the citizens of Lincoln County, and others, the sheriff (or his or her designee) may conduct a review of the special event and determine the additional security personnel required for matters such as traffic control, parking, security, or safety.
(b) Not less than ten business days prior to the said special event an application for the event shall be filed with the sheriff's office. Prior to the event, the sheriff's office shall notify the clerk of the commission of Lincoln County, and the chairman of the board of commissioners of the event. (2) Each deputy sheriff or security officer shall be paid for a minimum of four hours regardless of the duration of the event.
(3) In the event that security personnel are needed beyond four hours, each deputy sheriff or security officer employed for the special event shall be paid per hour for any increment of an additional hour worked.
(4) Payments shall be made directly to the deputy sheriff, or security officer, and shall be paid in United States currency.
(5) The minimum hourly rate for security personnel shall be set by the sheriff.
(d) A special event shall be defined for this chapter as "any festival, gathering, event, fair, or meeting organized or arranged for purposes of sport, religion, exhibition, trade, commerce, entertainment, music, industry, or any other purposes".

Additionally, the alcohol license holder shall be subject to prosecution in the Magistrate Court of Lincoln County. This division shall be known as the "Dog Control Ordinance."
